title: True a wobbly bicycle wheel
instruction: Adjust the spoke nipples to leave the bicycle wheel running straight and freely rotating.
context: Bicycle mechanics correct a wheel by finding the wobble and redistributing spoke tension without making the wheel loose or off-centre.
setup: Proposed fixed setup in setup.json: a 420 mm aluminium rim with 32 steel 2 mm spokes and 12 mm brass nipples, mounted upright in a single-sided steel truing stand. Two adjacent same-side nipples start 0.75 turn loose. The free steel spoke key with a polymer grip is 243 mm overall, with a 3.25 mm slot, 175 mm neck, 55 mm grip and 195 mm slot-to-grasp distance. The candidate robot layout clocks the wheel by 55° and phases its square flats by 45°. Exact geometry and coordinates are listed; complete native robot repair and its final setup screenshot remain unvalidated.
scoring: 0.5 for at most 1.5 mm peak-to-peak lateral runout; 1.0 for at most 0.5 mm. Both require a complete released revolution, radial runout at most 1 mm, dish error at most 0.5 mm, and every spoke within the specified fixture tension range of 400–1000 N. Check tension with a mechanical spoke tensiometer and its steel/2 mm conversion chart. Measure after both hands and the key are clear. Damage, direct rim bending, any support touching the rim during the judged revolution, invalid evidence or any other outcome scores zero. Proposed limits await stable full-scene verification.
run_limit: Proposed 2,400 control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz). The complete slow service compiles to 1,630 actions; the planned release-and-spin finale adds 391. Neither a full native run nor the final limit is validated.
reset_notes: Restore the same documented nipple rest lengths and intact wheel. Initial wobble is created by uneven spoke rest lengths, not a bent rim animation.
fidelity: A flexible rim and tensioned steel spokes respond to physical nipple rotation. The thread model changes spoke rest length by 0.454 mm per turn and applies equal and opposite reaction torque. Native contacts must grip and turn the free key. Elastic rim limits stop unsupported damage; stripped threads and permanent rim damage are not rendered. The passive corrected-state control passes, but full robot tightening and released rotation remain unverified.
scores: Development trials only. No full-score demo, Dream baseline or media exists. This is not submission metadata.
